title: Recarbonizing Global Soils
content: Increasing soil organic carbon through appropriate soil management can improve soil structure, soil health and water-related functions. The magnitude of change depends on climate, soil type and management conditions.

title: Soil Organic Cover
content: Maintaining soil cover protects soil from degradation, supports soil organisms, contributes to nutrient cycling and can improve soil structure and biodiversity.

title: Agroforestry
content: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock. Appropriate agroforestry systems can contribute to soil health, water regulation, habitat provision and biodiversity.

title: Conservation Agriculture
content: Crop diversification and maintaining soil cover are important components of conservation agriculture and can support soil biological activity, nutrient cycling and ecosystem functions.

title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity
content: Land-use change is a major pressure on biodiversity. Changes in habitat extent and condition can affect species populations and ecosystem functions.

title: Climate Change and Land
content: Climate change, land degradation, land management, biodiversity and sustainable land management are interconnected. Environmental interventions should consider these interacting factors rather than treating them independently.

title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
content: Habitat modification and land-use change can reduce biodiversity by changing habitat availability and ecological conditions.

title: Water and Soil Management
content: Soil organic matter and appropriate vegetation management can influence soil water retention and resilience to water stress. Management should be adapted to local climate and soil conditions.
